summary: This is a Gazebo Answers forum page (archived, read-only) for the question "How to do quadcopter simulation with Gazebo?" asked March 21, 2018 by user SimulationRookie. The asker has a mathematical quadcopter model and wants to simulate it in Gazebo, controlling individual rotor speeds and logging position and orientation to compare with their model. The accepted-style answer by josephcoombe points to resources (a YouTube video, the hector_quadrotor ROS wiki, and PX4 Gazebo simulation docs) and advises implementing aerodynamic models yourself in a plugin. The page notes the site is deprecated in favor of Robotics Stack Exchange.
one_line: Archived Gazebo Answers thread where a user asks how to simulate and control quadcopter rotor speeds in Gazebo, with suggested resources.
key_facts: The Gazebo Answers site (answers.gazebosim.org) was deprecated as of August 11, 2023, and users were directed to robotics.stackexchange.com.
The site remains online in read-only mode during the transition.
The question "How to do quadcopter simulation with Gazebo?" was asked on Mar 21, 2018.
The asker, SimulationRookie, is completely new to Gazebo and has developed a mathematical model for a quadcopter.
The asker wants to control the rotor speeds for the individual motors of a simulated quadcopter.
The asker wants to log x, y, z, and roll, pitch, yaw information from the simulation to compare with their own model.
The asker asks whether Gazebo has a ready-made quadcopter model and whether they should write their own plugin to control rotor speed.
The answer by josephcoombe was posted on Mar 23, 2018 and was updated the same day.
The answer recommends a YouTube video, the ROS wiki page for hector_quadrotor, and the PX4 Gazebo simulation documentation.
The answer advises that the user will probably have to implement the aerodynamic models themselves in a Plugin.
The question had been seen 12,817 times as of the page capture.
The asker thanked Joseph in a comment dated Mar 24, 2018.
The related questions list includes topics such as attaching cameras to quadcopter models, aerodynamics plugin parameters, and propeller rotation problems.
